findings.text: DESIGN QUESTION 1 (ready-transition-only enforcement) - SOUND, not under-scoping. O6's measure literally names 'the elaboration and validator refuse a behavior-bearing spec that declares no observability criteria'; the builder wired exactly that (the /warp:spec elaboration skill asks for the classification, and observability_gate refuses at validate.check_ready, the surface the skill runs before promoting to ready). This is deliberately NOT wired into frontier.claimable or plan.py run-check. That contrast with PLAN-0011's placement gate is correct and load-bearing: WARP-1103's outcome O3 explicitly demanded 'never claimed for build', which is why it touched frontier.py (the fleet area), spanned two areas, and was therefore a HIGH-risk, human_approval-required change. O6 carries no equivalent claim-gate language, so wiring the claim path would cross W9 into the fleet area and escalate its footprint tier to high and its risk to human-approval-required WITHOUT serving O6 - a scope and risk expansion the plan does not ask for. RESIDUAL (marginal, honestly documented in the spec Out-of-scope and manifest assumptions): because the gate does not re-fire at claim/build, a behavior-bearing spec whose observability block is stripped AFTER it reaches ready would not be caught mechanically at claim time. This is the same theoretical exposure the placement gate had before O3 forced belt-and-suspenders, it is caught in the review lane and by the footprint-vs-diff gate (the spec file re-entering the change set), and it is a legitimate cost/benefit call. Non-blocking.

DESIGN QUESTION 2 (behavior_bearing absent = exempt) - ACCEPTABLE trade-off, not a blocking hole. Absent/false = exempt is what preserves RJ6 (the 121 shipped specs declare no such field and are never gated) and is consistent with how the method treats every self-declared decision field: risk and placement are equally dodgeable by mis-declaration and are backstopped by the mandatory independent fresh-context review (C1), which this plan makes non-optional. The apparent dodge - a new author omitting the field on a truly behavior-bearing change - is NOT closed by the stricter alternative the builder weighed (defaulting absent -> gated / requiring an explicit true|false at ready): a dishonest author simply writes behavior_bearing:false instead of omitting, converting a silent omission into an affirmative false declaration, both of which are review-lane-caught dishonesty. Since whether a change is behavior-bearing is inherently a judgment (the module says so explicitly), NO gate keyed on that field can be made mechanically un-dodgeable; the method's uniform answer is the independent review, and this organ is consistent with it. The stricter default would also add real cost: it forces EVERY new spec (including pure-docs changes) to declare behavior_bearing:false to reach ready, and it would churn the existing check_ready selftests. I note one marginal improvement worth recording for a future item - forcing an explicit true|false classification at ready would make a dishonest exemption an affirmative act rather than an omission, slightly more legible to the reviewer and to audit - but it is a trade-off choice on the adoption-friction curve, not a defect. Non-blocking.

NO VACUOUS OR WEAK TESTS FOUND. The selftest's anti-vacuity tooth (line ~9864: 'elif not declared:' -> 'elif False:', fixture flips green, disk byte-unchanged) is genuine - I reproduced it independently against the on-disk module and it turns red under enforcement and green under mutation. The C7, RJ6, byte-identity, capability, and no-detach assertions are all load-bearing (each has a matching control or mutation). The honest mechanical/review-lane boundary (NG5) is respected: the gate enforces the floor and vocabulary and does not grade sufficiency, and that boundary is stated in both the module source and the spec.

summary: WARP-1209 (diagnosability gated, W9 of PLAN-0012) PASSES WITH NOTES at 379063b with ZERO blocking findings. The build ships exactly the diagnosability half of O6: a four-term observability criteria vocabulary (warp.observability/v1), a pure structural validator, and a mandatory gate that refuses a behavior-bearing spec declaring no observability criteria - all in the non-protected engine, byte-identical across root + plugin/templates + 6 packs, the /warp:spec skill in lockstep, the metrics half correctly left to W10 and the init lay-down to W11. I independently reproduced the gate GREEN (verify.sh exit 0), selftest 2103 passed / 0 failed, validate.py all exit 0 over the 121-shipped corpus, the RJ6 grandfathering (mandatory rule at check_ready only, never in run_all/check_spec; WARP-1103 check_ready == 0), the full anti-vacuity teeth (refusal by name, a byte-verified in-memory mutation that turns the fixture green, positive and negative controls), and all three C7 paths with the real contract standing down honestly. No protected path is touched and architecture.yaml is untouched. Both design questions resolve in the build's favor: ready-transition-only enforcement is a SOUND reading of O6's measure that correctly avoids a fleet-area crossing and risk escalation O6 does not require, and behavior_bearing-absent-as-exempt is an ACCEPTABLE, method-consistent trade-off whose stricter alternative closes no mechanical hole while adding adoption friction. Confidence: high.
